# osero-spusds-monitoring

A small read-only API that reports the performance of **Osero's ALM Proxy** allocation into
**SparkLend spUSDS** — the yield generated by that allocation from inception to now, the cost of
funds owed to Sky on it, and therefore whether the position actually makes money.

| | |
|---|---|
| Holder | [`0x6d37…b884`](https://etherscan.io/address/0x6d370e359e9cbd0fd35bb38faf705d84238cb884) (Osero ALM Proxy) |
| Position | [`spUSDS`](https://etherscan.io/token/0xc02ab1a5eaa8d1b114ef786d9bde108cd4364359) — "Spark USDS", SparkLend aToken, 18 dp |
| Underlying | [`USDS`](https://etherscan.io/token/0xdC035D45d973E3EC169d2276DDab16f1e407384F) |
| Pool | [`0xC13e…E987`](https://etherscan.io/address/0xC13e21B648A5Ee794902342038FF3aDAB66BE987) (SparkLend) |

---

## How the yield is calculated

SparkLend is an Aave v3 fork, so `spUSDS` is an **aToken**: the balance rebases upward as interest
accrues. Internally a holder owns a fixed *scaled* balance, and the displayed balance is

```
balance = scaledBalance × liquidityIndex / 1e27
```

The `scaledBalance` moves **only when principal moves**; all interest arrives through the index.
That gives an exact separation of principal from yield:

```
principal moved at block B = (scaled(B) − scaled(B−1)) × liquidityIndex(B) / 1e27

yield since inception      = current balance + everything ever withdrawn − everything ever deposited
```

### Why not just add up the Transfer events

Because it would be wrong. On a supply or withdraw, Aave folds the interest accrued since the
holder's last interaction into the `Transfer` value it emits (`amountToMint = amount + balanceIncrease`).
Summing those amounts would count part of the earned interest as fresh principal, inflating deposits
and understating yield. This service uses Etherscan's transfer list **only to discover which blocks
the position changed at**, then re-derives every amount from scaled balances read at those blocks.

Sanity check against the live position: the reconstruction returns the deposit as exactly
`1000000.000000000000000000` USDS, and the derived APR matches the reserve's own spot supply rate
to within a basis point.

### Returns

- `timeWeightedReturnPct` — compounded growth of the reserve index over the intervals the position
  was actually funded. Unaffected by the size or timing of deposits, and periods when the position
  was empty are excluded.
- `aprPct` / `apyPct` — money-weighted: yield over the *average capital deployed*, weighted by how
  long each amount was deployed, then annualised.
- `spotSupplyAprPct` / `spotSupplyApyPct` — the reserve's current supply rate, i.e. forward-looking
  rather than realised.

---

## How the cost of funds is calculated

Yield alone doesn't say whether the allocation makes money — the USDS was borrowed from Sky and
carries interest. A prime agent pays the base rate only on the **deployed** part of a
SparkLend/Aave position: the share of what it supplied that the pool has actually lent out. The
unborrowed remainder sits idle in the aToken contract and is deducted.

```
lendingIdle_d = position_d × poolIdle_d / totalSupply_d
deployed_d    = position_d − lendingIdle_d      ≡  position_d × utilization_d
baseRate_d    = ssrApy_d + spread_d
cof_d         = deployed_d × [(1 + baseRate_d)^(1/365) − 1] × dayFraction_d
```

`poolIdle` is the underlying token balance held by the aToken contract — the pool's unborrowed
liquidity. Cross-checked against the reserve's variable debt token, `totalSupply − poolIdle` matches
total borrows to within 0.007% (the gap is `accruedToTreasury`).

Evaluated on a **daily UTC grid**, reading the SSR on-chain at each day's block so rate changes are
picked up automatically. The first and last days are prorated, so a position opened at 08:35 is
charged 0.6422 of that day rather than a whole one.

**Net profit** = gross yield − cost of funds, reported on `/performance` and per-point on
`/performance/history`.

Rates are annualised against the **time-weighted average position** over the window, not the
position as it stands now — otherwise a position that grew would look cheaper than it was, and one
that has closed would divide a real cost by the 1 wei Aave leaves behind. `aprPct` is `null` when
there was no capital to measure against.

### Two conventions worth knowing

**The spread is additive here.** `baseRate = ssrApy + spread`, so 3.52% + 20bps = 3.72% exactly.
The settlement-cycle accounting repo combines them multiplicatively (`combine_apys`:
`(1+ssr)(1+spread)−1`), which is ~1.2bps higher. On $1M that's ~$7/year. This is deliberate — don't
expect a penny-exact tie-out against a settlement figure.

**The spread is date-keyed.** Sky moved it 30bps → 20bps on 2026-07-23, so a single constant would
misprice any window spanning that date. The schedule lives in `config.spreadSchedule` and is
overridable via `BASE_RATE_SPREAD_SCHEDULE`.

### Scope: bottom-up, not the settlement allocation

settlement-cycle charges the base rate on prime-level **ilk debt** and then allocates that charge
across venues pro-rata. This service computes a **standalone, bottom-up** cost for one position —
the number that answers "is Osero making money on this allocation?". The two agree only when the
position is funded 1:1 by ilk debt. No subsidy is modelled (Osero has none).

---

## Endpoints

### `GET /performance`
The main one. Current snapshot: principal in/out, current balance, **yield since inception**,
**cost of funds**, **net profit**, and realised APR/APY alongside the pool's spot rate.

```jsonc
{
  "position":  { "holder": "0x6d37…", "market": "SparkLend", "aToken": {…}, "underlying": {…} },
  "inception": { "blockNumber": 25601435, "date": "2026-07-24T08:35:11.000Z", "transaction": "0xff40…" },
  "asOf":      { "blockNumber": 25627048, "date": "2026-07-27T22:10:47.000Z" },
  "principal": { "totalDeposited": {…}, "totalWithdrawn": {…}, "netDeposited": {…} },
  "balance":   { "current": {…}, "scaled": "963390878287623295381362", "liquidityIndex": "1.0382066…" },
  "yield":     { "sinceInception": { "raw": "198813589948998028901",
                                     "formatted": "198.813589948998028901",
                                     "value": 198.81358994899801 },
                 "sinceInceptionPct": 0.019881 },
  "returns":   { "daysHeld": 3.566389, "timeWeightedReturnPct": 0.019881,
                 "aprPct": 2.034746, "apyPct": 2.055382,
                 "spotSupplyAprPct": 2.034924, "spotSupplyApyPct": 2.055769 },
  "flows":     [ { "date": "2026-07-24T08:35:11.000Z", "direction": "deposit", "amount": {…} } ],

  "costOfFunds": {
    "sinceInception": { "formatted": "223.455002493252001239", … },
    "aprPct": 2.263471,
    "averagePosition": { "formatted": "1000126.71441571053590001", … },
    "convention": "baseRate = ssrApy + spread (additive)",
    "basis": "deployed only — the pool has not borrowed out the idle remainder",
    "current": { "ssrApyPct": 3.52, "spreadBps": 20, "baseRateApyPct": 3.72,
                 "utilizationPct": 61.9727,
                 "position": {…}, "lendingIdle": {…}, "deployed": {…} }
  },
  "net": { "sinceInception": { "formatted": "-22.62002640107363439", … },
           "aprPct": -0.229128,
           "profitable": false }
}
```

Every amount comes as `raw` (wei, exact), `formatted` (decimal string, exact) and `value`
(JS number, convenient but lossy — use `formatted` for accounting).

### `GET /performance/history?interval=day`
Cumulative yield, cost of funds and net profit from inception to now, as a time series. `interval`
is `hour`, `day` or `week`; optional `from` / `to` (unix seconds) or `fromDate` / `toDate` (ISO),
and `limit` (default 400 — the series is thinned evenly if the range would exceed it). Each point
carries `balance`, `netDeposited`, `cumulativeYield`, `periodYield`, `aprPct`, plus
`cumulativeCostOfFunds`, `periodCostOfFunds`, `cumulativeNet` and `periodNet`.

### `GET /cost-of-funds`
The day-by-day breakdown, with every input to the charge — position, pool total supply, pool idle,
utilization, lending-idle deduction, deployed base, SSR, spread, base rate, day fraction, daily and
cumulative cost. This is the endpoint to read when you want to see the mechanics rather than the
headline:

```
date               blk    frac    util%        deployed   ssr%  bps   base%       cof       cum
2026-07-24    25606052  0.6422  61.9728      619,750.18   3.52   20    3.72     39.83     39.83
2026-07-25    25613233  1.0000  61.9728      619,784.70   3.52   20    3.72     62.02    101.85
2026-07-26    25620417  1.0000  61.9714      619,804.98   3.52   20    3.72     62.03    163.88
2026-07-27    25627307  0.9604  61.9727      619,851.47   3.52   20    3.72     59.57    223.46
```

### `GET /performance/at?date=2026-07-26T00:00:00Z`
The same snapshot as `/performance`, at a past point in time. Accepts `date`, `timestamp` (unix
seconds) or `block`. Dates before inception return a zeroed position; dates in the future clamp to
the latest block.

### `GET /flows`
Every principal deposit and withdrawal detected on the position, with amounts and tx hashes.

### `GET /health`
Liveness probe — also confirms the RPC is reachable.

## Deploying on Railway

1. Push this repo to GitHub, then **New Project → Deploy from GitHub repo** in Railway.
2. Set the two variables under **Variables**:

   | Variable | Value |
   |---|---|
   | `RPC_URL` | your Ethereum mainnet RPC URL |
   | `ETHERSCAN_API_KEY` | your Etherscan API key |

3. Deploy. `railway.json` already sets the start command and points the healthcheck at `/health`.
   Railway injects `PORT` automatically — don't set it.

Optional variables (all have sensible defaults):

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `HOLDER_ADDRESS` | Osero ALM Proxy | Track a different holder |
| `ATOKEN_ADDRESS` | SparkLend spUSDS | Track a different aToken (any Aave v3 style market) |
| `CHAIN_ID` | `1` | Etherscan v2 chain id |
| `LIVE_CACHE_TTL` | `30` | Seconds to cache live chain reads |
| `RPC_CONCURRENCY` | `4` | Max in-flight RPC requests |
| `RPC_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` | `50` | Minimum gap between RPC requests |
| `SUSDS_ADDRESS` | sUSDS mainnet | Where the SSR is read from (`ssr()`) |
| `BASE_RATE_SPREAD_SCHEDULE` | 30bps → 20bps on 2026-07-23 | Spread over SSR, as JSON: `[{"from":"2026-07-23","bps":20}]` |

### Running locally

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env      # fill in RPC_URL and ETHERSCAN_API_KEY
node --env-file=.env src/server.js
```

### Tests

```bash
npm test
```

39 unit tests over the money math in `src/math.js` and `src/cost.js` — the lending-idle identity,
the additive base rate, wei-exact rate application, day-grid proration, the spread-schedule
boundary, cumulative-cost interpolation and cache bounding. They run **offline**: no RPC key, no
Etherscan key, no network. CI runs them on Node 20 and 22.

---

## Requirements and limits

- The RPC must support **archive `eth_call`** (historical state). Alchemy's free tier does.
- `eth_getLogs` is *not* used, because free RPC tiers cap it to a handful of blocks — hence the
  Etherscan dependency for discovering the position's flow blocks.
- Historical chain state is immutable, so anything keyed by a concrete block is cached in memory
  forever; only "latest" reads carry a TTL. The cache is per-instance and lost on redeploy.
- Cold start costs ~2 archive calls per historical flow. That is instant for this position (one
  deposit so far), but a position with hundreds of flows can exhaust a free RPC tier's throughput;
  the service throttles and backs off, and returns `503` with a clear message if the limit still
  bites. A paid RPC endpoint removes the ceiling.
- The cost-of-funds series costs **one multicall per calendar day** the position was open. Past
  days are cached permanently, so only the current day is re-read; a first request after a redeploy
  on a year-old open position issues ~365 multicalls. Same throttle, same `503` fallback. A closed
  position stops the grid at the flow that emptied it, so it costs days-held, not days-since-
  inception.
- The in-memory cache is LRU-bounded (`CACHE_MAX_ENTRIES`, default 20,000). Keys embed block
  numbers, so an unbounded map would grow for as long as the process lives.
